protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; RULE-GOVERNED mechanics entry under user-made adopted D-054
summary: The subject never matched the dispatch. It measures cab483b5 and the dispatch pins bb806328, stable across four measurements a second apart, 83 lines, mtime 11:18, untracked and not written by me. No file in the D-057 set carries the dispatched digest. The dispatch states 'This subject is FROZEN. If it moves, OBJECT', so I object on that alone. I nonetheless reviewed the bytes that exist so the work is not wasted, and on those bytes every named attack fails: the entry disclaims granting anything and points authority at adopted D-054, forbids same-commit bundling, requires the DR-005 rider by name, and its ten eligible-row pairings and three exclusions all reproduce against the adopted register. Both cited digests match live, including a COORD pin correctly refreshed to the post-D-054 value. If the dispatched bytes are re-issued and they are these bytes, I expect to consent.

objections.claim: The subject is not the dispatched artifact. The review therefore cannot bind the bytes the dispatch names, and no independent review exists for those bytes.
evidence: The dispatch pins bb8063282404df905c976aa1cb237f8fcf4667d7ceff5def8eadaffb7835c863 and states 'This subject is FROZEN. If it moves, OBJECT.'

docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-057.draft.md measures cab483b5493f98588b471a55eb3688e3146767bc295bf51667ab92fa3f417bdc, identical across four consecutive measurements taken a second apart, so it is stable rather than mid-write.
It is 83 lines, 3332 bytes, mtime Aug 14 11:18, untracked. My filesEdited is empty and git reports zero modified tracked files, so the divergence is not mine.
No other file in the D-057 set carries the dispatched digest: the draft is cab483b5 and the review prompt is 6359436c.
The divergence predates my review rather than occurring inside it: start and end measurements are identical. The subject was already not the dispatched bytes when I first measured.
objections.whyItIsABlockerRatherThanAnAdministrativ: This corpus adopts digests, not intentions. An adopted entry cites a reviewer verdict against a subject digest so a later reader can confirm the review happened on the adopted bytes. If D-057 were adopted at bb806328 citing this verdict, it would record a review that never occurred on those bytes; if adopted at cab483b5, it would cite a dispatch that pinned something else. Either way the audit chain breaks at the one link it exists to protect. The dispatch anticipated exactly this and instructed OBJECT.
objections.remedy: Re-dispatch with the digest of the bytes actually under review, or restore the bytes the dispatch pinned. Then this cycle can proceed against a subject a reviewer can bind.
objections.patternWorthNaming: This is the second consecutive entry in this family with a subject-freeze failure. On D-054 turn 1 the subject moved during review, from 7d10d8f4 to 0224356d, which I recorded as C2-D054-02; here the subject never matched the dispatch at all. The turn-2 dispatch for D-054 responded by making subject motion an explicit MUST-FIX and that subject did hold, so the control works when it is applied. It needs to be applied to the dispatch-to-first-measurement window as well, not only to the review window.

substantiveReviewOfTheBytesThatExist.result: No MUST-FIX and no SHOULD-FIX found in the content. Every named attack fails.
findings: The attack 'this entry itself grants owner authority (must remain D-054)' fails, and the entry is structured around refusing it. The decision-type line reads 'Mechanics only. Authority is user-made adopted D-054, not this file', the header carries '**Does not** grant owner authority', clause 1 is titled 'This file does not grant' and states 'Adopted D-054 is the user amendment that permits preview-scope owner recording. This entry only states how later D-000 owner-recording entries must be written. Overturning this entry does not overturn D-054', and the alternatives reject 'Repeat the grant in this file.' The separation is stated four times and the reversibility clause keeps it: 'C-D057 revokes these mechanics. D-054 remains until C-D054.'

The attack 'this entry itself discharges condition 1' fails: clause 6 states 'This entry records no row. Readiness effect zero. File 08 is not edited here', and the Readiness effect section repeats 'Zero.'

The attack 'silent SATISFIED' fails: the header carries '**Does not** mark SATISFIED', clause 4 states the later owner-recording 'may not mark the row `SATISFIED`', and clause 5 mentions SATISFIED only as DR-001's existing standing.

The attack 'same-commit coordinator + owner recording' fails twice: clause 2 requires the coordinator recording to be 'already ADOPTED and separately committed (D-000 clause 4)' and states 'Same-commit bundling of the coordinator recording and the owner recording is forbidden', and the alternatives reject it citing D-000 clause 4.

The attack 'owner record of DR-005 v2 without RB-DR005-V2-A1' fails three times: clause 3 states 'DR-005 is v2 plus RB-DR005-V2-A1', clause 5 lists 'DR-005 (D-028; D-039 plus RB-DR005-V2-A1)', and the alternatives reject omitting it citing D-039. I confirmed the rider is genuinely in adopted D-039, which is the entry I reviewed when it was drafted.

The attack 'grant extends to DR-006/007/009 before their selections' fails on verified fact, not on the sentence: clause 5 states they 'enter only after their Route B selections are adopted', and I searched every adopted entry — none selects Route B for DR-006, DR-007 or DR-009.

The attack 'grant extends to DR-010 or condition 5' fails: clause 5 states 'DR-010 remains Route C', which matches D-001's route assignment, and clause 4 forbids the later recording from authorizing docs/v2/implementation/, with the header carrying the same refusal.

All ten eligible-row pairings in clause 5 reproduce against the adopted register: DR-002 with D-047 and D-049, DR-003 with D-030 and D-041, DR-004 with D-048 and D-050, DR-005 with D-028 and D-039, DR-008 with D-029 and D-040 — every one an adopted entry naming that row.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails: COORD fb1189620f7ac653d0d92c0fe223e3854806336a5738da70e2580ffad96b89a5 and file 08 6547e6ace2ae61e664af0f65059b66c2cb3d0539d64f6687aba04f8f54dc4cd7 both match live, and D-054's adoption commit 29670ed exists in git log. The COORD pin is notably the refreshed post-D-054 value rather than a carried-forward one.
The attack 'file 08 edited' fails: git reports docs/v2/architecture and COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md clean with zero modified tracked files.

Clause 3's required-pin list is specific and auditable: file-08 owner role, disposition path and sha256, both verdict paths and sha256s, preview scope, Route A remainder, coordinator-recording decision ID and commit, and every operative rider or binding advisory, with an explicit rule that an ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES case 'must classify each advisory as non-operative or carry it into the owner record'. That last clause closes the gap where an advisory could be silently dropped between the disposition review and the owner record.

Reversibility is the correct compound form and correctly severed from D-054: 'C-D057 revokes these mechanics. D-054 remains until C-D054. Undoing effects also requires superseding every owner recording that cites D-054/D-057 and reconciling each dependent MF-6 note under its own reviewed act.'

whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of this subject. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.
The bytes the dispatch pinned at bb806328. They do not exist anywhere I can find, so I cannot say how they differ from the bytes I reviewed or whether my substantive findings would carry to them.

Whether adopted D-054 in fact confers the authority this entry's mechanics presuppose. D-054 is not my subject here; it was adopted at 29670ed while its own turn-2 review was in flight, and I recorded my objection to that draft separately. This entry correctly points at D-054 rather than re-granting, so the question of D-054's own sufficiency travels with D-054.

The 'claimed turn-1 repairs not landed' axis in the dispatch. This file is labelled turn 1 and cites no prior verdicts, so there are no turn-1 repairs of its own to verify; the repairs it embodies are those of the superseded D-054 drafts, which I checked in that cycle.

nonConsentNote: I do not CONSENT, on one MUST-FIX, and it is procedural rather than substantive. The dispatch said the subject is frozen and to object if it moves; the subject I measured was never the subject the dispatch named, stably and from the first measurement. I reviewed the bytes that exist anyway, and they are good: the entry refuses to grant, points authority at adopted D-054, forbids same-commit bundling, requires the DR-005 rider in three places, and every factual claim I could test reproduces against the adopted register. My objection is that a verdict must bind bytes someone can re-derive, and right now the dispatch and the file disagree about which bytes those are. Re-dispatch at the true digest and, on this content, I expect to consent.
